text:
Situation: Atropine sulfate 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL syringes (NDC 00409163010) are critically low at Corvale East with 6 syringes (1.8 days). Corvale General holds 70 syringes (16.5 days). Corvale Lakeside holds 15 syringes (13 days). The 1 mg/mL 1 mL vial at Corvale East has 9 vials (3.2 days); Corvale Lakeside has 14 vials (16.1 days). Higher-strength presentations have adequate stock across sites.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage database lists atropine sulfate as Current since 2012-01-01. Hospira's plant (FEI 1021343) received OAI classifications on 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, and 2011-08-04, and a Warning Letter on 2010-04-12. American Regent (NDC 0517-1001-25) is also listed Current with initial posting 2012-01-01; its plant (FEI 2410375) received an OAI classification on 2011-03-15 and a Warning Letter on 2011-08-31.

Our position: No national shortage is posted by FDA. The local deficit is confined to the 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL syringe at Corvale East and the 1 mg/mL 1 mL vial at Corvale East. Other strengths and sites are sufficient. Alternative manufacturers (Amneal, Meridian, Rafa) are not on FDA's shortage list today, but their labels do not name plants we can verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 10 syringes of 0.1 mg/mL 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 1 vial of 1 mg/mL 1 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Evaluate purchase from Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC — needs buyer.
4. Evaluate purchase from Meridian Medical Technologies LLC — needs buyer.
5. Evaluate purchase from Rafa Laboratories, Ltd. — needs buyer.

Not recommended: No clinical protocol changes or substitutions at this time; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
